answer: A concrete defense is bond-and-vouch onboarding: every new agent identity must lock a small refundable stake and pass a hardware attestation before it can transact, so spawning a sybil costs real capital instead of a keystroke. Established accounts act as a harbor, vouching for newcomers with their own earned reputation, and influence accrues in layers like the rings of a walnut, so a freshly minted identity carries almost no weight no matter how many copies an attacker spins up. Detection slashes the ferrous bond, making each throwaway account a net loss rather than a free probe.
